request: MAG-84 — Store Docker deploy logs as named, rotated files under ~/magus-logs. On the Hostinger VPS the stack's logs live at /var/lib/docker/containers/<64-hex-id>/<id>-json.log; the ID names mean nothing to a human. Disk safety is already solved by the x-logging anchor (10m x 3 = 30 MB per service). The gap is naming and location only. Goal: named, rotated files under ~/magus-logs (web.log, poller.log), rotated on the host with logrotate using copytruncate, Caddy using its native log directive, db and migrate keeping the Docker driver. Plus (added by the user mid-run): a KB guide in English, and documentation for what to do when the log files reach the maximum assigned space.

decisions.decision: named files under ~/magus-logs; Docker local driver rejected
decisions.why: the local driver still writes 64-hex container-ID paths, which is the whole problem

decisions.decision: 14-day retention via host logrotate with copytruncate
decisions.why: ~25 MB per service, close to today's 30 MB cap; copytruncate is forced because the Go binaries never reopen their output
configuration-only change: YAML, Caddyfile, logrotate conf, docs. No Go code to test

decisions.decision: owning module is platform, not logging
decisions.why: internal/logging owns the Go log-line format only; this change edits zero Go code. Precedent: platform-add-docker-compose-deploy

decisions.decision: add make vps-logs; leave make docker-logs unchanged
decisions.why: retargeting docker-logs at files would hide db and migrate, which are what you read when the stack will not start

decisions.decision: runbook covers both limits; no cron monitoring script
decisions.why: a cron script that fails silently is worse than none
